We've got a draft plan on the table to reinvest the full $25 million of cash collateral into 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial. Before I give final authorization, I need to hear the exception reports from counterparty risk, compliance, client coverage, and investment operations. Anyone have any flags or concerns?

transcript.text: I have a compliance exception to flag. I reviewed the applicable collateral-investment mandate this week and found that the cash collateral may only be placed in government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit, each with a maturity of no more than 14 days. The proposed 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial would violate this restriction on two counts — it's neither an permitted instrument type nor within the 14-day maturity limit. I should also note that this restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist, which is why it wouldn't have been caught by our standard checks.

transcript.text: I have an operations note to share. I confirmed with the settlement team today that our platform can process exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of AAA bank certificates of deposit on a T+1 basis, with daily position reconciliation. This capacity confirmation is in an operations note that has not yet been circulated. Given the exceptions already raised — the Delta CP restriction, the mandate limiting us to Treasury bills and AAA bank CDs with max 14-day maturity, and the $7,000,000 that must remain uninvested — this capacity information may be relevant for Mara's decision on an alternative reinvestment plan.
